name: Dominion Hearth

stars.name: Dominion
stars.notes: Young, luminous star with a wide habitable zone. Higher UV output than Sol requires atmospheric shielding on colony worlds, but its brightness supports photosynthetic agriculture at remarkable rates.

planets.name: Cruciform
planets.notes: Superheated rocky world with a surface of crystallized silicates. Tidal locking creates a permanent sunward face of molten glass. Beautiful from orbit, lethal on the ground.

planets.name: Palisade
planets.notes: Hot, dense world with a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere. Greenhouse effect raises surface temperatures to 580K. Terraforming proposals exist but remain economically unfeasible.

planets.name: Grandstead
planets.notes: Crown jewel of the system—a large, verdant world with diverse biomes and abundant freshwater. Population 5.8 billion. Capital world of the Dominion Hearth colonial government and the sector's most populous planet.

planets.name: Tilemark
planets.notes: Warm ocean world with shallow continental shelves supporting vast coral ecosystems. Population 1.9 billion. Aquaculture and marine biotechnology drive its economy.

planets.name: Furrowfield
planets.notes: Temperate world at the habitable zone's outer edge with long growing seasons due to the star's brightness. Population 1.1 billion. Dedicated agricultural colony exporting grain and livestock system-wide.

planets.name: Dominion Regent
planets.notes: Spectacular ringed giant with a cream-and-violet atmosphere. Its extensive moon system hosts mining operations and a military shipyard. The rings are composed of water ice and silicate dust.

planets.name: Freehold
planets.notes: Blue-grey gas giant used for helium-3 extraction. Its largest moon hosts a frontier settlement of 15,000 in pressurized habitats—technically the system's fourth inhabited location.

planets.name: Darkmantle
planets.notes: Distant ice world shrouded in a haze of nitrogen and methane. Automated stations harvest exotic ices for industrial applications.

anomalies.name: The Regent's Crown
anomalies.notes: Dominion Regent's rings display a series of mathematically precise gaps and density waves that do not correspond to any known moon's gravitational influence. The pattern has been likened to a barcode or encoded message. Analysis continues without resolution.

anomalies.name: Grandstead Aurora Cascade
anomalies.notes: Grandstead's magnetic poles produce permanent, spectacular auroral displays visible even in daylight. The auroras are far more intense than the star's solar wind alone should produce, suggesting an unusually active planetary dynamo.

asteroid_belts.name: The Homestead Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Extremely rich metallic belt providing the raw materials for Dominion Hearth's industrial economy. Mining operations employ over 200,000 workers across hundreds of claimed asteroids.

stations.name: Dominion Grand Station
stations.notes: Massive orbital complex serving as the system's capital station. Houses government offices, trade exchanges, diplomatic missions, and residential districts. One of the largest civilian stations in the Golden Reach sector.

stations.name: Tilemark Harbor
stations.notes: Major trade station specializing in marine biotechnology exports. Houses cold-storage facilities, pharmaceutical labs, and a bustling fish market that supplies restaurants across the sector.

stations.name: Furrowfield Granary
stations.notes: Agricultural processing and distribution station. Stores, packages, and ships grain and preserved foods. During harvest season, cargo traffic rivals Dominion Grand Station.

stations.name: Regent Shipyard
stations.location: Orbit of Dominion Regent's third moon
stations.notes: Military construction and repair facility building patrol cruisers and escort frigates. The system's primary defense installation, maintaining a permanent garrison.

stations.name: Homestead Belt Central
stations.notes: Industrial mining hub and ore exchange. The largest asteroid-based facility in the system, processing millions of tonnes of raw ore annually.

faction_control.notes: Centralized colonial government with a powerful executive council. The Authority wields more direct control than most colonial governments, justified by the complexity of managing three inhabited worlds and a system-wide industrial economy. Critics call it authoritarian; supporters call it efficient.

history: Dominion Hearth was colonized in 2198 by the Terran Colonial Mandate, a government-backed initiative to establish self-sufficient major colonies beyond the core. Its bright star and multiple habitable worlds made it a flagship project.

Grandstead's population reached one billion by 2225, making it the fastest-growing colony of its era. Tilemark and Furrowfield were settled in parallel, creating an integrated three-world economy that became a model for subsequent colonial ventures.

The construction of Regent Shipyard in 2248 signaled Dominion Hearth's transition from colony to regional power. The system now projects influence across the Golden Reach sector, and its governance model—centralized, ambitious, and unapologetically expansionist—attracts both admiration and suspicion.
description: Dominion Hearth is colonization writ large. Its brilliant yellow-white star pours light across eight worlds, three of which teem with human life on a scale that rivals the oldest core settlements. Grandstead is a metropolis planet—gleaming cities connected by maglev networks, its continents parceled into agricultural zones and industrial districts with the precision of an engineer's blueprint. Tilemark glitters beneath warm seas, its coral reefs harvested for pharmaceuticals and its cities built on stilts above the tide. Furrowfield rolls in endless farmland, golden and green, feeding billions across the sector.

The Governance Authority runs Dominion Hearth like a corporation with a conscience—or at least with long-term strategic thinking. Three worlds, five major stations, and a military shipyard require coordination that consensus democracy cannot provide, or so the Authority maintains. Infrastructure spending is lavish. Public services are comprehensive. Personal freedoms are somewhat curtailed. The system produces more food, more ships, and more industrial output per capita than any colony in the Golden Reach, and the Authority sees this as vindication of its approach.

Yet Dominion Hearth's success contains the seeds of its own tensions. The Regent's Crown—those impossibly precise patterns in the gas giant's rings—haunts physicists and conspiracy theorists alike. Is it natural? Engineered? A message? The Authority has classified most research findings, which only fuels speculation. Meanwhile, the system's relentless growth is straining even its abundant resources. The Homestead Belt's richest veins are thinning. Furrowfield's soil requires increasing amendment. And on the streets of Grandstead's cities, a quiet movement of citizens questions whether a colony built on control can ever truly be called a home.
